LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoBeds_Detail: {0} sleep on the ground. Even {1} would stop the nightly mood penalty.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Barracks_Detail: {0} would sleep better (and be happier) in rooms of their own.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_FoodLow_Title: Food runs out in about {0} days
LanguageData.CC_Adv_FoodLow_Detail: Hunt, forage, harvest anything ripe, or buy food from traders. Cooking meals stretches raw food further than eating it raw.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Winter_Title: The growing season ends in about {0} days
LanguageData.CC_Adv_WinterNow_Title: Lean season: about {0} days until crops grow again
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Winter_Detail: You have about {0} days of food. To get through the {2}-day cold spell you'll want around {1}.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Winter_Hydro: A greenhouse with {0} would let you grow food all year.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Winter_NoHydro: Plant more now, hunt before the animals migrate, and trade for food.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Freezer_Title: Food is spoiling without a freezer
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Freezer_Detail: {0} pieces of perishable food are stored warm. A closed room kept below freezing with {1} keeps it fresh.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Spoil_Detail: {0} pieces of perishable food are stored warm. Eat perishables first, store food in the coldest room you have, and don't overstock raw food in summer.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Spoil_Preserve: {0} pieces of perishable food are stored warm. Turn surplus into {1}, which keeps far longer, and eat perishables first.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cold_Detail: You have {0} heat source(s). Plan {1} for the bedrooms and workrooms before the cold arrives.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_WarmClothes_Title: {0} colonist(s) aren't dressed for the cold
LanguageData.CC_Adv_WarmClothes_Detail: {0} will be uncomfortable at {1}. Make warmer clothes (parkas, tribalwear, dusters) before then.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Hot_Detail: You have {0} cooler(s). Plan {1} for the bedrooms to prevent heatstroke.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Defense_TitleBad: Your defenses may not hold the next raid
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Defense_Detail: Raids are currently worth about {0} points. You have {1} fighter(s), {2} turret(s), {3} trap(s) and {4} pieces of cover.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Defense_Growth: Colony wealth grew {0} in the last 15 days, so raids will grow too.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Defense_Suggest: Next step: about {0} more {1}, placed where raiders approach.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Defense_SuggestTrain: Next step: better weapons and some shooting practice.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoDoctor_Detail: Enable Doctor in the Work tab for at least one colonist, ideally your best at Medicine.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Medicine_Detail: Buy medicine from traders, or research how to make it. Even a few doses save lives.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Medicine_Grow: Grow {0} to make herbal medicine, and buy better medicine when traders visit.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Hospital_Detail: After one bad raid, the injured will lie wherever they fall. A small hospital (a few beds set to "medical") is a lifesaver.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_PowerShort_Title: The power grid is running out
LanguageData.CC_Adv_PowerShort_Detail: The grid uses about {0} W more than it produces and the batteries are nearly empty. Add generators or switch things off.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_SolarOnly_Detail: Every night (and every eclipse) the power goes out. Batteries or a second kind of generator fix that.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoBattery_Detail: Batteries store surplus power for when generators dip. Handy for freezers.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoPower_Title: The colony has electricity research but no power
LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoPower_Detail: Something like {0} would power lights, better workbenches and coolers.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Rec_Title: Recreation is thin ({0} kinds, colonists want {1})
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Rec_Suggest: Adding {0} would give them something new ({1}).
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Dining_Detail: Colonists eat without a table and lose mood at every meal. Put {0} and some chairs in a room.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Work_Detail: Nobody is assigned to {0}. Check the Work tab.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Rot_Detail: Items left under the open sky slowly fall apart. Put a roof over your stockpile.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Rot_DetailShelf: Items left under the open sky slowly fall apart. A roofed room with some shelving ({0}) fixes it.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Research_Detail: Suggested next project for your era: {0} (cost {1}).
LanguageData.CC_Idea_RecRoom_Title: Idea: a room just for fun
LanguageData.CC_Idea_RecRoom_Detail: A dedicated recreation room gives a mood bonus every time someone relaxes there.
LanguageData.CC_Idea_Dining_Title: Idea: dress up the dining room
LanguageData.CC_Idea_Dining_Detail: A more impressive dining room gives a mood boost after every meal. Floors, art and good furniture help.
LanguageData.CC_Idea_Barn_Title: Idea: give the animals a barn
LanguageData.CC_Idea_Barn_Detail: Animals sleeping outside get cold and sick. A barn with sleeping spots keeps them healthy.
LanguageData.CC_Idea_Era_Detail: Your colony is settled. Research like {0} opens new possibilities.
LanguageData.CC_Idea_Empire_Detail: The Empire hands out titles for favours. A noble colonist brings powerful perks, and expensive tastes.
LanguageData.CC_Wishes_None: Nobody is asking for anything right now. Enjoy it while it lasts.
LanguageData.CC_WishesDisabled: Wishes are switched off in the mod settings.
LanguageData.CC_Listen_Tip: Ask around. If anyone has a wish, they'll speak up now. (Once a day.)
LanguageData.CC_Listen_Cooldown: You already asked today. Give them some time.
LanguageData.CC_Listen_Nothing: You asked around, but nobody wants anything right now.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Short_Gentle: Gentle mode: granted wishes lift mood, ignored ones cost nothing.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Short_Balanced: Balanced mode: granting helps, ignoring stings, and others notice who gets what.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Short_Demanding: Demanding mode: broken promises and favoritism bite hard, and bitter colonists may sulk.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Short_AdvisorOnly: Advisor-only mode: wishes are suggestions, with no mood effects.

LanguageData.CC_Alert_WishesDesc: These colonists are waiting on a wish. Granting it lifts their mood; ignoring it costs nothing in Gentle mode.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EnableAdvisor: Advisor: rank what the colony needs
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EnableAdvisor_Tip: Shows prioritized, explained advice on the Council tab's Priorities page.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EnableWishes_Tip: Colonists voice wishes based on their traits, passions, relationships and mood.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EnableAmbitions_Tip: Every so often the council meets and colonists pitch a bigger goal for the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EnableTouches_Tip: Colonists occasionally plan a small piece of furniture for their own bedroom (as a normal blueprint you can cancel).
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Gentle_Tip: Only upsides. Granted wishes and achieved ambitions lift mood; ignoring a wish, refusing it or failing an ambition costs nothing. Trust is still tracked, but only its good side has effects.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Balanced_Tip: Upsides and downsides. Ignored wishes and refusals sting, broken promises sting more, colonists who waited longer feel passed over, the jealous resent favorites, and ignored colonists can turn disgruntled and work slower. Granted wishes can leave people motivated.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Demanding_Tip: Like Balanced, with every penalty 50% stronger. Bitter, unhappy colonists may storm off to sulk or go on an insulting spree.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_AdvisorOnly_Tip: No mood effects from this mod at all. Wishes and ambitions are pure suggestions.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_ForOthers: Kind colonists can ask on behalf of others
LanguageData.CC_Settings_ForOthers_Tip: A kind colonist may notice someone else's hardship and ask for them. Both are happier if it's granted.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Petitions_Tip: Colonists who want the same thing back each other's wish instead of making a new one.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_WishLetters_Tip: Off: new wishes appear as short messages instead.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_GrantedLetters_Tip: Off (default): a short message when a wish comes true.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_SpeechText_Tip: Shows a short line above a colonist when they make, back or get a wish, or pitch an ambition.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_AdvisorAlert_Tip: Shows the council's most urgent concern in the alerts on the right.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_WishAlert_Tip: Shows a reminder in the alerts while colonists are waiting on wishes.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Jealousy_Tip: When a wish comes true, the jealous, the greedy, rivals and those who have waited longer may resent it, and some will ask for the same thing.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EventWishes_Tip: Raids, deaths, cold nights, meals eaten off the floor and the like make colonists speak up within hours, about the thing that just happened.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Reminders_Tip: Halfway through, colonists bring their wish up again; near the end they make a last, pointed call.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_SelfHelp: Colonists take matters into their own hands
LanguageData.CC_Settings_SelfHelp_Tip: Hard-working, handy colonists who run out of patience sometimes sort it out themselves: they plan the lamp, switch their own work back on, mark out a grave, pick an animal to tame.
LanguageData.CC_Promise_Tip: Tell them you'll see to it. They wait half again as long and trust the council a little more. If it doesn't happen in time, it's a broken promise: much worse than never promising.
LanguageData.CC_Refuse_Tip: Say no, honestly. It stings now (less for kind or ascetic colonists) but it's over: no reminders, no slow souring, and they won't ask again for a long while.
LanguageData.CC_Refuse_Confirm: Refuse {PAWN_nameDef}'s wish for {WISH}? It will disappoint {PAWN_objective}, and {PAWN_pronoun} won't ask for it again for a while.
LanguageData.CC_LastCallMessage: {PAWN_nameDef} is running out of patience about {WISH} ({TIME} left).
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Plan: Tired of waiting, {PAWN_nameDef} planned {THING} for the room {PAWN_pronoun} sleeps in. The builders will find the blueprint; cancel it if you object.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_ShareBed: {PAWN_nameDef} has moved into {OTHER_nameDef}'s bed. Nobody asked the council. Nobody had to.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Grave: {PAWN_nameDef} marked out a grave for {OTHER_nameDef}. Once it's dug, the body can be laid to rest.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Tame: {PAWN_nameDef} picked out an animal ({SUBJECT}) and marked it for taming. If {PAWN_pronoun} isn't allowed to handle animals, someone else will have to.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Work: {PAWN_nameDef} switched {PAWN_possessive} own {SUBJECT} work back on. You can switch it off again in the Work tab, if you're willing to have that conversation.
LanguageData.CC_PromiseKeptNote: A promise kept. {PAWN_nameDef} won't forget it.
LanguageData.CC_Trust_Sub: Grows when wishes come true and promises are kept; falls when they're ignored, refused or broken. Trusting colonists are patient and content; bitter ones grumble, stop asking and (on Demanding) may sulk. Hover a name for the history.
LanguageData.CC_Trust_Tip: {0}: trust {1}\nGranted {2}, let go {3}, refused {4}\nPromises kept {5}, broken {6}
LanguageData.CC_Chronicle_SelfHelp: {0} stopped waiting for {1} and saw to it alone.
LanguageData.CC_Chronicle_PassedOver: {0} colonist(s) felt passed over when {1} got {2}.
LanguageData.CC_Almanac_AllDlc: Show pages for DLCs I don't have
LanguageData.CC_Adv_ButcherInKitchen_Detail: The {0} shares a room with the stove. Butchering spatters blood and makes the kitchen filthy, and filthy kitchens make food poisoning far more likely. Move it to its own room next door.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_DirtyKitchen_Detail: Kitchen cleanliness is {0}. Below -2, dirt starts adding to the chance of food poisoning. Have someone clean it, and lay a proper floor if it's bare ground.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoCleaner_Detail: No colonist has Cleaning switched on. Filth will pile up in the kitchen, hospital and dining room, dragging down mood and health. Give it to someone in the Work tab.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_DirtyHospital_Detail: Hospital cleanliness is {0}. Dirt raises the chance of infections and failed surgery.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Fire_Rooms: {0} room(s) have an open flame inside wooden walls.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Fire_Walls: {0} of the colony's walls are wooden.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Fire_Detail: One stray spark and it all goes up. Rebuild the walls around fires, storerooms and bedrooms in {0}.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Infestation_Detail: {0} cells of the home area lie under overhead mountain. Hives can appear there when it's warmer than -17 °C, preferring dark spots far from open sky. Walling up unused mountain rooms (every second tile is enough) prevents them.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Infestation_Turret: A {0} or two covering the deep rooms would help when they come.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Infestation_LowTech: Keep fighters with good melee weapons near the deep rooms, and don't store anything precious there.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Corpses_Detail: Seeing the dead sours everyone's mood, and the smell of rot is worse.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Corpses_GraveOrBurn: Bury colonists in a {0}; burn strangers in a {1} or dump them far away.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Corpses_Grave: Bury them in a {0}, or set up a dumping stockpile far from the base.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Corpses_Dump: Set up a dumping stockpile far from the base, out of sight.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Blight_Detail: Blight spreads to nearby crops. Cut the blighted plants now, before it takes the whole field.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_HarvestFrost_Detail: It's {1} outside and getting colder, and {0} plants are ripe enough to harvest. Frost kills crops; harvest them now.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Expectations_Detail: About {0} more wealth and everyone's expectations rise to "{1}": their mood cushion shrinks, and they'll want {2} kinds of recreation. Make sure moods can take it, or spend wealth on things that make people happy.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_NoWarden_Detail: {0} prisoner(s), and no colonist has Warden work switched on. They won't be fed, talked to or recruited.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_HungryPrisoner_Detail: {0} is close to starving. Check that a warden can reach the cell and there's food to bring.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_PrisonerBed_Detail: Prisoners need a prisoner bed in a cell. Without one they sleep on the floor and grow harder to recruit.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Dark_Detail: Colonists in the dark work slower and get a mood penalty. {0} in each would fix it.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_ToxicFallout_Detail: Poison is falling from the sky ({0} left). Everyone outdoors slowly builds up toxic buildup. Restrict colonists to roofed areas, bring animals inside if you can, and expect outdoor plants to die.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_VolcanicWinter_Detail: Ash dims the sun for a long while ({0} left): it's colder and crops grow slower. Stock extra food and fuel.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_SolarFlare_Detail: Electrical devices are dead ({0} left). Freezers warm up, hydroponics wither and turrets fall silent. Keep the freezer door shut and fighters ready.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_HeatWave_Detail: Dangerous heat ({0} left). Keep colonists indoors in cooled rooms during the hottest hours, watch for heatstroke, and keep the freezer closed.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_ColdSnap_Detail: A sudden freeze ({0} left). Harvest what's ripe, warm the bedrooms, and dress people properly before they go out.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_Flashstorm_Detail: Lightning without rain ({0} left): fires will start. Keep firefighters at home and stay clear of dry brush.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_PsychicDrone_Detail: A drone grinds on the minds of one gender ({0} left). Watch moods: give recreation time, good food and rest to those affected.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_NoxiousHaze_Detail: Polluted haze ({0} left). Keep people indoors where you can; it harms lungs over time.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_Drought_Detail: The land is parched ({0} left). Crops grow poorly; lean on stores, hunting and trade.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_Eclipse_Detail: The sun is gone for a while ({0} left). Solar panels are useless and outdoor crops stall; lean on batteries and other power.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Cond_Aurora_Detail: Lights dance across the sky ({0} left). Colonists who see it feel better; a good night for a walk outside.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Birthday: {PAWN_nameDef} turns {AGE} in the next couple of days.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_ArtInRoom_Artist: {PAWN_nameDef} is an artist with nothing beautiful in {PAWN_possessive} own room.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_ArtInRoom: {PAWN_nameDef}'s expectations have grown, and {PAWN_possessive} room has no art.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_DayOff_Tired: {PAWN_nameDef}'s recreation is almost empty and {PAWN_possessive} schedule barely allows any.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_DayOff_Lazy: {PAWN_nameDef} is not one for hard work, and the schedule has noticed.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_LittleSomething: {PAWN_nameDef} has a taste for chemicals, and the colony has almost none in stock.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Recruit: {PAWN_nameDef} has taken a liking to the prisoner {OTHER_nameDef}.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Tidy: {PAWN_nameDef} counted {COUNT} patches of filth in the home area and has opinions about it.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Tidy: {PAWN_nameDef} picked up a broom and made cleaning {PAWN_possessive} top priority. You can change it back in the Work tab.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Music: {PAWN_nameDef} has music in {PAWN_objective} and nothing to play it on.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Armor: {PAWN_nameDef} fights for the colony with no real armor, and the colony could make some.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Wedding: {PAWN_nameDef} marked out a marriage spot for {PAWN_objective} and {OTHER_nameDef}. Once it's built, the wedding can happen.
LanguageData.CC_Rooms_Hint: Click a room to plan it. Right-click to plan it at a good spot. Highlighted rooms are what the council is asking for.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_RoomsButton: Show the "rooms" button in the bottom bar
LanguageData.CC_Settings_RoomsButton_Tip: A shortcut to all room plans. The same plans are always in the council's Build tab.
LanguageData.CC_Floor_OnlyAffordable: Only floors we have the materials for ({0} tiles)
LanguageData.CC_Floor_Hidden: {0} more floor type(s) hidden: not enough materials for the whole room.
LanguageData.CC_Floor_Hint: Hover for costs. Floors are laid after the walls go up.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Justice: {PAWN_nameDef} hasn't forgiven the raid, and {OTHER_nameDef} is the only raider still breathing.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_JusticeBlood: {PAWN_nameDef} is bloodthirsty, and {OTHER_nameDef} is sitting in a cell doing nothing about it.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_JusticeGrief: {PAWN_nameDef} is grieving, and blames {OTHER_nameDef}'s people for it.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_JusticeCold: {PAWN_nameDef} sees no use in feeding {OTHER_nameDef} any longer.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Justice: Set {OTHER_nameDef} to be executed in the prisoner tab, or leave it.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Mercy: {PAWN_nameDef} is kind, and thinks keeping {OTHER_nameDef} locked up has gone on long enough.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_MercyChild: {PAWN_nameDef} can't stand seeing a child like {OTHER_nameDef} behind bars.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_MercyHurt: {PAWN_nameDef} has seen the state {OTHER_nameDef} is in, and wants them let go.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_MercyFriend: {PAWN_nameDef} has become friends with the prisoner {OTHER_nameDef}.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Mercy: Release {OTHER_nameDef} (or recruit them) from the prisoner tab.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Party: {PAWN_nameDef} thinks the colony is overdue for some fun.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_PartyGloom: The whole colony is miserable, and {PAWN_nameDef} thinks a party would help.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Party: Promise it and the council calls a party right away. Otherwise, wait for one.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_NoGatherSpot: A party needs somewhere to gather: build a party spot, or a table people can sit at.
LanguageData.CC_Promise_Party: The council calls a party, and {PAWN_nameDef} is throwing it.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Party: {PAWN_nameDef} got tired of waiting and started a party {PAWN_objective}self.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Rescue: {OTHER_nameDef} was carried off by {FACTION}, and {PAWN_nameDef} can't stop thinking about it.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Rescue: {OTHER_nameDef} is held by {FACTION}. Bring them home: a rescue, a ransom, or a trade.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Hunt: {PAWN_nameDef} loves to shoot and has been eyeing the wildlife.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_HuntBlood: {PAWN_nameDef} is bloodthirsty and wants something to kill. Better an animal than a colonist.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Hunt: Mark an animal for hunting and let {PAWN_nameDef} do the Hunting work.
LanguageData.CC_Promise_Hunt: The council marks a {SUBJECT} for {PAWN_nameDef} to hunt. Make sure {PAWN_pronoun} is allowed to hunt in the Work tab.
LanguageData.CC_SelfHelp_Hunt: {PAWN_nameDef} picked out a {SUBJECT}, marked it for hunting and grabbed {PAWN_possessive} gun.
LanguageData.CC_QuittingText:
{PAWN_nameDef} has been bitter about the council for days and has had enough. Unless something changes in the next three days, {PAWN_pronoun} will pack up and leave the colony for good, taking whatever {PAWN_pronoun} is carrying.
Granting one of {PAWN_possessive} wishes, or keeping a promise, can win {PAWN_objective} back.
LanguageData.CC_StayingText: {PAWN_nameDef} no longer feels ignored, and has decided to stay.
LanguageData.CC_QuitText: Nobody listened, so {PAWN_nameDef} walked out, and is no longer part of the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Chronicle_Quitting: {0} announced they were leaving the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Quitting: Bitter colonists may leave the colony (Demanding stakes only)
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Quitting_Tip: A colonist who stays bitter for days warns that they're leaving, and walks out three days later unless their trust recovers. Children, and anyone whose partner is staying, never leave.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Standards: Rising standards: the happy grow harder to please
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Standards_Tip: While colonists are happy, their standards creep up: the council's mood rewards shrink, letdowns sting more, and wishes come more often and ask for more. Hard times, and the austerity decree, bring standards back down.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Standards: {PAWN_nameDef} has grown used to comfort, and the bedroom doesn't feel good enough any more.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_StandardsFood: {PAWN_nameDef} has grown used to good food. Simple meals don't cut it any more.
LanguageData.CC_Standards_Tip: Standards: {0}. They rise while {1} is happy and fall in hard times. The higher they are, the less the council's rewards lift {1}'s mood, the more letdowns sting, and the more {1} asks for.
LanguageData.CC_Decrees_Sub: Spend the colony's good mood on what it needs, or the other way round. Up to {0} decrees at a time. Everyone reacts according to their nature, and living under a decree they hate wears down their trust.
LanguageData.CC_Decree_EnactedText: The council has declared {0} for the next {1}.
LanguageData.CC_Dilemma_Deadline: The council has {0} to decide. If nobody does: "{1}".
LanguageData.CC_Dilemma_BreakReason: The council's answer was too much.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Dilemmas: Council dilemmas: hard choices now and then
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Dilemmas_Tip: Every so often the council has to settle something: a thief, a feud, a forgotten stash, a confession. Every answer costs someone something. They come more often while everyone is happy.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Annals: Yearly annals: a colonist writes up each year
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Annals_Tip: When a new year begins, the colony's best reader or talker writes up the year that ended: who came, who was lost, raids, the council's decisions, friendships and feuds. Past years can be reread from the Chronicle tab.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Opening: The year {0} is over. {PAWN_nameDef} sat down by the fire and wrote it all down, so that somebody would remember.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_OpeningPartial: The year {0} is over. {PAWN_nameDef} wrote down what the council saw of it, from the day it began keeping records.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Count: We began the year as {0} and end it as {1}.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Died: {0} did not live to see the new year.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Gone: Gone from us, but not dead as far as we know: {0}.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_NoRaids: Nobody came to kill us this year. Nobody.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Raids: Trouble came {0} time(s): raiders, beasts, worse.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Richer: We grew richer: the colony was worth about {0} silver at the start of the year and {1} now. Somebody will have noticed.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Poorer: We grew poorer: from about {0} silver of worth to {1}.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Steady: The colony's worth held about steady, near {1} silver.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Wishes: The council granted {0} wish(es) and let {1} slip away.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Ambitions: Ambitions achieved: {0}. Ambitions failed or abandoned: {1}.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Dilemmas: The council was asked to settle {0} hard question(s).
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Rivals: Worst of enemies: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}. Keep them on different shifts.
LanguageData.CC_Annals_Devoted: Nobody trusts the council more than {PAWN_nameDef}.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Outside: {PAWN_nameDef} hasn't been outdoors in far too long.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Outside: Give {PAWN_nameDef} outdoor work or recreation: hauling, hunting, growing, a walk.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Fix: {PAWN_nameDef} is addicted to {DRUG} and the stores are running low.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Quit: {PAWN_nameDef} is addicted to {DRUG} and wants to get clean.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Quit: Keep {PAWN_nameDef} away from {1} (Assign tab, drug policy) until the addiction passes.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Separate: {PAWN_nameDef} shares a bedroom with {OTHER_nameDef} and can't stand {OTHER_objective}.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_Separate: Give {PAWN_nameDef} or {OTHER_nameDef} a bed in another room.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_Infirmary: {PAWN_nameDef} counted the medicine: {COUNT} doses for the whole colony.
LanguageData.CC_Log_RepealIgnored: asked for {0} to be lifted, nobody listened
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DecreeRequests_Tip: When the moment fits (food running low, right after a raid, while people grieve, when everyone is spoiled), a colonist who would like a decree asks the council for it. Declaring it within a few days wins their trust; ignoring it costs a little.
LanguageData.CC_Anniversary_One: It has been a year since {PAWN_nameDef} joined the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Anniversary_Many: {PAWN_nameDef} has been with the colony for {YEARS} years.
LanguageData.CC_Anniversary_Old: {YEARS} years: {PAWN_nameDef} is one of the colony's old hands now.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Anniversaries: Mark each year a colonist has been with the colony
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Anniversaries_Tip: On each anniversary of joining, the colonist says a few words, feels remembered, and their friends share it.
LanguageData.CC_Goal_NoRivals: No two colonists who can't stand each other ({0} pair(s) now)
LanguageData.CC_Goal_ColonyTrust: The colony's trust in the council at {0} or more (now {1})
LanguageData.CC_Goal_NoAddictions: Nobody addicted to anything ({0} addicted now)
LanguageData.CC_Epithet_FirstRound: The colony already has names for some of its people: {0}.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Epithets: Colonists earn names for what they do (the Healer, the Kindling...)
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Epithets_Tip: Whoever has done the most of something (tended wounds, killed raiders, cleaned messes, caught fire) earns a name for it, until someone overtakes them.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Spoiled_Title: The colony has grown hard to please
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Spoiled_Detail: {0} of {1} colonists are spoiled. Rewards barely lift their mood, letdowns hit hard, and they keep asking for more. Austerity, or a little hardship, resets it.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Leaving_Detail: {PAWN_nameDef} will walk out in {TIME} unless their trust recovers. Grant one of their wishes or keep a promise.
LanguageData.CC_Adv_Bitter_Detail: Bitter: {0}. They work slower, break sooner and have stopped expecting anything.
LanguageData.CC_Reason_PetBed: {PAWN_nameDef} is bonded to {OTHER_nameDef} and wants {OTHER_objective} close at night.
LanguageData.CC_Progress_HurtAnimal: {OTHER_nameDef}: {1} health. Make sure a doctor is allowed to tend animals.
LanguageData.CC_Goal_RaidSettlement: Destroy a hostile settlement (nearest: {0} of {1}, {2} tiles away)
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Journals_Tip: Each colonist writes a line in their own voice when something happens to them: wishes granted or ignored, promises, decrees, raids, losses, names earned. Click a name in the Wishes tab's trust list to read it.
